processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five different alloys synthesized in one operation using five movable Cu molds filled successively from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock; after cooling and cutting, blocks were 10×50×130 mm³.
10×50×130 mm³ blocks hot rolled into 2±0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets reheated to 1100 °C and water quenched.
Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into nine segments of 2×60×55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Scales removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 µm and some retained microsegregations of Mn (after hot rolling and water quenching).

XRD screening of the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl class indicates austenite with increasing ferrite content as Al rises (2–11 wt.%); the mechanical trend correlates more with ferrite content than with κ-carbides or ε-martensite.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: all plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl, increasing ferrite content appears more relevant for the mechanical trend than κ-carbides or ε-martensite.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure investigation; check for cracks, pores, macrosegregations
characterization_methods.key_findings: no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and retained Mn microsegregations.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl TWIP steel class, yield strength and ultimate tensile strength both increase while tensile elongation drops as Al content increases in the range 2–11 wt.%; XRD screening indicates increasing ferrite content is more relevant for this trend than κ-carbides or ε-martensite [b0026].
The RAP aging matrix used 450, 500, 550, and 600 °C for 0 h, 1 h, and 24 h each, followed by oil quenching (45 sample conditions); the present sample corresponds to the 450 °C/1 h condition [b0020].
No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations were found in the final RAP materials; the as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure [b0021].

Figure 6 reports Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl mechanical/XRD data only for as-quenched and 24 h aging conditions (400/500/600 °C), so no numeric YS/UTS/TE/hardness values specific to the 450 °C/1 h condition are available in this text [figure_006].
